idiom_name: marker (lazy initialization, virtual proxy, value holder or ghost) plus a loader that runs through the session
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep the identifier (or whatever construction/fetch needs) on the object, put a marker where the value belongs, and route every access through one accessor. The accessor checks the marker, calls the loader - a mapper or gateway method that knows the store and runs through the session - stores the result and returns it. Choose the marker by what callers must see: a sentinel field (lazy initialization) when the object is yours, a stand-in with the same interface (virtual proxy) when clients must not see the difference, a getValue()-style holder when the load should be explicit, or a ghost (identity-only real object) when the loaded value must be the object's own type. Always route the load through the session/identity map, decide what happens on failure (retry or cache) and what invalidates the loaded value, and prefer declaring the policy once in the mapping rather than at every use site.
code_sketch:
book.author                          # accessor: is the marker empty?
  value = gateway.find(book.author_id)   # load through the session
  book.author = value                    # cache: never load again
  return value
# marker forms: null sentinel | virtual proxy | value holder.getValue() | ghost
pitfalls: Loading outside the owning session/transaction: the marker is only loadable while the context that can execute the read still exists.
Conflating 'not loaded' with 'absent': a sentinel that doubles as a legitimate value either re-queries forever or hides a missing row.
Letting every access trigger its own query instead of caching once - or caching and never defining what invalidates the value.
Wrong move: iterate every parent and touch its lazy collection -> the ORM emits one query per parent (N+1) -> instead selectinload, join-fetch or project the needed shape before iteration.

Wrong move: return entities with unloaded associations after closing the session -> lazy access fails with a detached-object error -> instead materialize a DTO or projection inside the transaction or keep an explicit load boundary.

Wrong move: let JSON serialization, toString or a getter traverse lazy associations -> rendering performs hidden I/O or cascades through the graph -> instead serialize a bounded DTO and make any prefetch explicit.
